text:
evan: Heads up — after rolling gpu-operator v1.12.0 in us-west-2 we started seeing nodes report 0 allocatable GPUs and scheduling failures. rolling back in-progress ops now.
maya: ugh. any error logs from device-plugin or kubelet?
evan: yes, from kubelet: `device plugin registration failed: timeout waiting for registration` and from nvidia: 
```
NVRM: The NVIDIA probe routine was not called for 1 device(s).
NVRM: No NVIDIA devices were found.
```
maya: that log smells like driver <-> kernel module mismatch / module load order. did the operator image change driver install ordering?
ops-bot: deploy event: gpu-operator/v1.12.0 rolled to 60% (canary nodes: gpu-canary-1). cluster: prod-usw2.
jasper: quick sanity: `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, alloc: .status.allocatable}'` shows many nodes with `nvidia.com/gpu: "0"` even though GPUs are physically present.
samir: are these nodes running the new device-plugin pod? if device-plugin fails the scheduler will see 0 allocatable. `kubectl -n gpu-system get pods -o wide`?
evan: device-plugin ds on affected nodes is CrashLoopBackOff. logs show `failed to initialize: driver mismatch detected: kernel module (530.30) != driver toolkit (530.14)`
lina: that's specific — where did the toolkit come from? operator bundle change?
maya: PR #4125 changed the driver-toolkit image tag to be pinned to `530.14` to match newer CUDA stack, but our nodes have a 530.30 kernel module from the kernel/AMI build. mismatch causes module load to be rejected by the plugin.
jasper: re: scheduling, pods show Pending with message: `0/120 nodes are available: 38 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 82 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate` — some new node-label/taint behavior landed in the operator too.
evan: i've started a canary rollback: `kubectl -n gpu-system set image daemonset/gpu-operator gpu-operator=redwood/gpu-operator:v1.11.7` then rolling restart. doing it on the canaries first.
maya: good. to patch quickly, you can also replace the device-plugin image with previous tag: `kubectl -n gpu-system patch daemonset nvidia-device-plugin --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/image","value":"nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:0.12.3"}]'`
evan: applying that now.
ops-bot: alert: 27 pods in namespace ml-models Pending for > 10m. affected: batch and realtime queues.
samir: we should avoid full cluster drain; instead cordon affected nodes then evict low-priority pods and leave infra daemons. `kubectl cordon <node>` + `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector='priorityClassName!=system-node-critical'`
lina: for capacity routing, can we add a nodeSelector to high-priority jobs to prefer nodes that haven't been upgraded (label `gpu.redwood/driver=530-30`) until this is resolved? That buys time.
jasper: we have ~150 reserved GPUs in us-west-2 Dedicated pools — if large fraction becomes unusable, cost vs SLAs will get ugly. ops: will customers see throttling?
evan: yes, some capacity-based throttles already hit for low-priority batch jobs. I'm coordinating with capacity team to re-home some jobs to us-east-1 where driver alignment is fine.
maya: long term fix: operator should detect kernel module vs toolkit mismatch preflight and avoid surfacing broken device plugin. open an issue to add guard that checks `modinfo nvidia` vs toolkit version and fails the rollout if mismatch.
samir: also add a post-install probe that runs `nvidia-smi` and `nvidia-container-cli --load-kmods` during the daemonset rollout; if probe fails, rollback automatically.
evan: filed infra-ticket INF-7321 and linked PR to revert v1.12.0.
ops-bot: rollback job started for gpu-operator -> v1.11.7 by evan at 1839006023.
deploy-bot: patch applied to nvidia-device-plugin on canaries. rollout status: progressing -> awaiting pods ready.
lina: action items: evan rollback + confirm device-plugin healthy on canaries; maya add preflight to operator; jasper coordinate capacity rehomes; samir craft drain/cordon runbook; I'll notify SRE/Sales if customer-facing queues degrade. :eyes:
evan: updating INF-7321 with logs + kubectl commands. will report back after canary verification (ETA 30m).
maya: thanks — if rollback doesn't fix it, we'll cut a kernel-compatible toolkit image and push a hotfix (short-lived).
evan: can confirm canary now reports `nvidia.com/gpu: "1"` and `nvidia-smi` returns GPUs. starting staged rollout. will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
